subject: Logic
title: Fermat's Last Theorem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fermat's Last Theorem.

hook.text: In 1637, Fermat scribbled that he had a marvelous proof—but the margin was too small. He never wrote it down.

buildup.text: The claim: no three positive integers a, b, c satisfy aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ for any integer n greater than 2.

discovery.text: For 358 years, the world's best mathematicians failed. Then Andrew Wiles locked himself away for seven years.

twist.text: Wiles's first proof had a flaw. He spent another agonizing year patching it before succeeding in 1995.

climax.text: The proof connected number theory to elliptic curves—an entirely unexpected bridge between distant math fields.

punchline.text: 358 years. One margin note. One proof.

quiz.question: Who finally proved Fermat's Last Theorem?
